### Decent Markdown Editor

This is a decent editor for Markdown. Works quite well, for both editing and previewing. My only complaint is that when I open a document, or create a new one, right after launching the app (including via opening documents from Finder) the window is extremely small, and the preview pane much smaller. I'd give this 5 stars once this issue is resolved.

results.title: Markdown Editor Mac: 8 Editors, Prices and macOS Needed
results.content:
### Is there a free Markdown editor for Mac?#

Yes. MacDown 3000, MarkEdit and MarkText are free and open source under the MIT license. Obsidian is free without limits, commercial use included. Cogito is free while it is in beta. Checked November 3, 2026. For free viewers too, and when a paid app is worth it, see free vs paid Markdown viewers on Mac.

### Does Mac have a built-in Markdown editor?#

No. TextEdit opens a `.md` file as plain text and does not render it. MarkEdit describes itself as just like TextEdit, dedicated to Markdown.

### Is there an open source Markdown editor for macOS?#

Yes: MacDown 3000, MarkEdit and MarkText, all MIT licensed with their source on GitHub. MarkText's macOS builds are unsigned, so macOS blocks them until you clear the quarantine flag. [...] The macOS version decides what you can run. Requirements go from macOS 10.15 to macOS 26: MarkEdit's current release needs 26, Cogito 15, MarkText 13, and MarkEdit's older releases start at 12. On a Mac stuck on Big Sur (macOS 11), only MacDown 3000, Typora and iA Writer remain.

"Editor" and "reader" get mixed up. Typora's page title reads "simple yet powerful Markdown reader", while its tagline says "A minimal Markdown editor and reader". Google's "People also ask" box for this search, the same day, included "What is the best Markdown viewer for Mac?". Plenty of people who type "editor" want to read Markdown. An editor works for that, but it opens every file ready to be changed.

## If you only need to read Markdown# [...] Free: everything, plus Shortcuts and AppleScript support and an extension manager. Its README says it collects no user data.
 Limit: the current release needs macOS 26; older Macs need one of its separate releases for macOS 12 to 15. It's a source editor: you see highlighted Markdown, not the formatted page.
 For: people who write raw Markdown and want the editor to stay out of the way.

My verdict: the best fit if TextEdit is what you wish you could use for Markdown. Install it from GitHub or Homebrew: the old address markedit.app now redirects to a different, paid product (AnnexEdit).

## MarkText: free WYSIWYG, but unsigned#
